metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Thailand

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results for Thailand based on the PISA 2022 Database. The factsheet does not provide the underlying microdata analysis code or explicit statements about applying student sampling weights or replicate weights; therefore, weight usage cannot be confirmed from the provided text. PISA results are produced using PISA’s complex survey design and scaling procedures, and the factsheet presents uncertainty intervals (95% confidence intervals) consistent with survey-aware estimation. Analysts using the PISA database should apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate-weight procedures (as documented in the PISA technical documentation) when reproducing standard errors and confidence intervals.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the provided document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking results (means, proficiency levels, and associations) rather than reporting an original student-level predictive model with an explicit PV estimation procedure. Missing-data handling is not reported in the factsheet text because it focuses on published summary statistics and does not describe any re-analysis pipeline or imputation/deletion rules.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports that, in Thailand, 8,495 students in 279 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science in 2022, and that the creative thinking cognitive test was implemented in 64 countries/economies including Thailand. The provided text does not specify additional analytic exclusions (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds) beyond the stated completion of the assessment.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Thailand’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment consists of 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). In Thailand, students scored a mean of 21 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average (33), and only 37% reached at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), compared with 78% on average across OECD countries. The factsheet also reports that 7% of students are top performers (Level 5 or 6), and that socio-economic status, gender, and several beliefs/attitudes are associated with creative thinking performance. It further notes COVID-19-related data collection challenges and provides guidance on interpreting estimates for countries/economies with unmet sampling standards.
